content:
Over the past year, we’ve been eagerly awaiting the launch of the next-generation iPad mini, and it looks like the wait is almost over. Last week, Aaron Perris revealed that the new device will feature the A20 Pro chip and slimmer bezels, and we also know it will sport an OLED display and a water-resistant design.

While all these upgrades sound great, my biggest hope for the next iPad mini actually has nothing to do with hardware — it’s about the software.

After seeing iPhone Duo in action, I’m blown away by how Apple has handled multitasking. Multitasking on the iPad has always felt like a mess to me, but iPhone Duo does it with such elegance.

On such a small screen, a full windowing system simply doesn’t make sense for the iPad mini. Users aren’t going to be stacking tons of overlapping windows on a device this size. So I’d love Apple to take a page from iPhone Duo and add one practical feature: split view plus picture-in-picture.

Comment by Mathew Ledbetter

You make a great point, and it echoes my biggest frustration — the software is just a shrunken-down version of the full-size iPad experience. Apple clearly hasn’t put much effort into tailoring the experience for this form factor. The widgets are absurdly tiny, and the home screen can only fit so many rows of icons, leaving huge gaps of empty space. It’s a genuinely poor experience.

Honestly, this experience is fantastic. Right now, there’s no way to expand a picture-in-picture window on the iPad mini so that it spans the full width of the screen in portrait mode — and even if you could, you’d either be covering parts of an app or fiddling around with the windowing system to resize things manually.

Bringing split video and app viewing to the iPad mini’s display feels like a no-brainer to me, especially given that the iPhone Duo and the iPad mini have similar aspect ratios. At least personally, if this feature existed, I’d use my iPad mini in portrait mode far more often.
